functionalObligations.text: an order is split across several venues by an off-chain algorithm that selects on price, slippage and cost, over both automated market makers and private market makers
functionalObligations.note: The splitting algorithm itself is closed; only its inputs and its named venue examples are published.

functionalObligations.text: quotes from private market makers are solicited off-chain and evaluated against on-chain venue quotes in the same selection
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Rf asserts a signed maker quote. OKX names PMMs as a quote class but publishes nothing about whether the quote is signed, whether it is firm, or whether the maker retains a last look. Carried, because the quote class is documented; marked, because its binding character is UNKNOWN. Contrast Jupiter F7, where last look is documented and Rf is therefore dropped.

functionalObligations.text: in intent mode the user signs a declaration to swap A for B under stated conditions rather than a transaction, the declaration is never exposed to the public mempool, and a settlement contract pays out at least the minimum stated in it or reverts and returns the tokens
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS, which decomposes OKX as {Ag, Rf}. All four parts of L12 are present: signed constraints, a settlement verifier, a solver set, and a bounded auction window with a fallback to the classic path. The corpus's category claim that the four intent symbols 'do not begin to differentiate anything until rank 6 and below' fails at rank 3.

functionalObligations.text: the signed intent is offered to competing solvers who bid for the right to fill it in an auction lasting about two seconds, and the best bid wins
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a considered departure from stage 1, which called this 'arguably Ba' on OKX's own phrase 'parallel batch auction'. Ba is batch-auction CLEARING: a uniform price computed over a batch of user orders. Here many solvers bid on ONE order, and no uniform price is computed across a batch of anything. The corpus's own CoW Swap row records the missing object precisely ('the auction being a price DISCOVERY device for a single order rather than a matching device across orders'), so rejecting Ba here is consistent with the corpus's own reading, not a novel one. The vocabulary has no symbol for a solver tournament over a single order.

functionalObligations.text: the bids in that auction are sealed, so no solver can see another's price before committing
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Sb is shielded-balance state and does not name bid privacy in an auction; nothing else comes near. Whether bids are sealed determines the auction's equilibrium and the decomposition cannot record it.

functionalObligations.text: only solvers on an operator-maintained allowlist may fill an intent, subject to onboarding requirements, performance standards and anti-manipulation controls set by the operator
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Solver eligibility stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. Aw was considered and is rejected under this lane's standing principle: Aw is used for gates on the party seeking the service and never for gates on who may fill someone else's order. The corpus already treats this as residue at 1inch ('no element for resolver whitelisting/staking as a barrier to solver entry'), so the reading is the corpus's own.

functionalObligations.text: solvers operated by or affiliated with the operator compete in the operator's own auction for the operator's own order flow, and the operator publishes a policy saying so
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol can express 'the operator is also a bidder', and none names a self-declared conflict as part of the mechanism. Published 2026-04-30, modified 2026-05-29; it is the single most useful primary document in this category because it is the only place any operator here states in writing what it does with the flow it controls. The disclaimers it makes (no preferential routing to affiliates, to the operator's venture portfolio, to protocols on the chain it owns, or to counterparties with revenue-sharing agreements) are themselves evidence that those relationships exist.

functionalObligations.text: the winning solver pays the settlement gas, so the user's cost of execution in intent mode is zero gas
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Gs). The corpus already uses Gs for exactly this shape at 1inch Fusion ('gasless swaps where the resolver pays settlement gas'). L21 (Gs implies Au plus metering plus fee settlement) is NOT discharged: the solver absorbs the cost as a cost of winning, with no delegated scope and no metering.

functionalObligations.text: the system, not the user, decides which of two incompatible execution regimes runs, on trade size, token classification and a user-chosen speed mode, and which party bears price risk between signature and fill changes with that decision
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest structural gap in this application. In and Ag name the two regimes; nothing names the dispatcher that chooses between them, and nothing can express that the location of price risk is a function of that choice. In classic mode the user bears it; in intent mode the winning solver bears it between its bid and its settlement.

functionalObligations.text: the operator's own route may be presented as the default selection or visually emphasised in the interface, including where its quoted received amount is not the highest available
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the purest case in the category of a mechanism the 58 cannot see, because it is not on-chain at all and yet determines where the majority of trades go. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief: the displayed route and the best route are conceded to be different objects. X14's second limb holds in the strongest available form, since the operator itself concedes the displayed route may not be best.

functionalObligations.text: a referrer commission is read out of the last words of the settlement calldata behind magic flags, capped by the router at 3 percent (10 percent on Solana), charged on one side of the trade only, deducted before execution, and paid to the integrator rather than to the operator
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Fd is the nearest and is rejected: Fd names distribution of a protocol's own surplus or fees, whereas this is a third party's cut of someone else's user, compiled into the settlement layer and capped by it (CommissionLib.sol: commissionRateLimit = 300, event CommissionRecord(uint256, address referrerAddress), FROM_TOKEN_COMMISSION / TO_TOKEN_COMMISSION flags). Order-flow monetization enforced on-chain for a beneficiary who is not the protocol has no symbol.

functionalObligations.text: the same routing engine is sold to other order-flow owners, powering swaps inside a rival wallet, and is supplied as one competing quote engine inside a rival aggregator
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the nesting finding. One Ag runs inside another Ag: OKX is simultaneously its own wallet's aggregator, MetaMask's aggregator (see https://web3.okx.com/learn/okx-dex-api-consensys, accessed 2026-08-05), and a quoting participant inside Jupiter's meta-aggregator. The vocabulary has no composition operator, so a flat corpus row cannot say that one row is a component of another; two members of this category's top eight are components of a third, and any construction treating them as independent will double-count.

functionalObligations.text: the user grants token allowance to a separate approval contract per chain, distinct from the router that spends it
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, same reading as LiquidMesh F17. L17's expiry and nonce or domain separation are absent; X16 is armed. Solana and TON require no approval, which the decomposition also cannot express.

functionalObligations.text: the identity of the settlement contract is not a constant: routers may be replaced on upgrade and integrators are instructed to use whatever address the API returns rather than hardcoding one
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Up (mutable implementation proxy) was considered and is rejected: the verified BSC deployment 0x6015126d7D23648C2e4466693b8DeaB005ffaba8 is a plain DexRouter and NOT a proxy, so mutability is achieved by deploying a new contract and changing what an off-chain API answers. No element names mutation of a mechanism by redeployment plus a redirect, which is strictly less accountable than Up because there is no on-chain upgrade event to observe.

functionalObligations.text: MEV-protected broadcasting is available only to customers the operator has approved by email application, on four named chains
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and residue in its substance. Aw carries only the gate on who may obtain the service; the object being gated, protection of a transaction's path to inclusion, has no symbol at all. Protection here is a commercial tier, not a property of the mechanism.

functionalObligations.text: a self-hosted routing client is distributed as a closed binary behind an API key and a whitelist form, computes routes locally from streamed pool state, and will additionally search for the most profitable round-trip across a set of intermediate tokens
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, twice. First, the canonical routing artifact is a Docker image with no source and no license (the repository contains a Dockerfile, a compose file and docs, and no code), which no element can express. Second, cyclic arbitrage routing means the router is also a searcher, sold as such; the vocabulary has no way to say that the thing routing your order is also hunting round-trips.

functionalObligations.text: a cross-chain swap behind the same interface moves the user's asset between domains by routing across third-party bridges the operator selects
functionalObligations.note: Xf IS DISCHARGED BY DELEGATION, not by OKX's own contracts: the routed-to bridge moves the value, and OKX supplies neither Xm nor a named custodian. Because the vocabulary has no composition operator, a construction cannot say 'Xf present by delegation', so stage 3 will see Xf without Xm and without L8's alternative. That verdict is the nesting finding restated by the checker, not a defect in OKX. The corpus residue 'no element for cross-chain swap routing as a distinct product' stands and is confirmed.

functionalObligations.text: the splitting algorithm, the private-market-maker set, the solver allowlist and the auction's conduct are all unverifiable from outside, and the canonical settlement repository the operator once published has been withdrawn
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. github.com/okx/WEB3-DEX-OPENSOURCE now returns HTTP 404 from the GitHub API and does not appear in the okx organisation listing; the code survives only in forks, of which the cited one carries Apache-2.0 at the root and SPDX MIT on individual files. No element expresses the evidentiary status of a mechanism, and with no versioned source of record there is nothing to diff a rotating deployment against.

functionalObligations.text: the operator stands on both sides of the order-flow market at once: it owns users through an exchange and a wallet, owns a chain, sells its engine to rivals who own users, sells the right to fill through an auction it also bids in, and hands the fee lever to integrators
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: the corpus claims OKX DEX decomposes identically to Binance Wallet. It does not. Binance Wallet is a pure demand-side owner with no sell-side product, no solver set, no published policy and no API; OKX is a supply-side vendor that also owns demand. Their economic positions are different in kind, and the corpus's identity claim {Ag, Rf} = {Ag, Rf} is an artefact of a vocabulary that names route construction and stops.

paper.title: OKX DEX
paper.label: cat:int:okx
paper.blurb: An exchange-operated aggregator that now runs a sealed auction over its own affiliated solvers, and publishes a conflict-of-interest policy conceding that it may display a route which is not the best available.
paper.witnessReason: The witness adds an intent element on evidence of the auction, and explicitly refuses the batch-auction element: many solvers bidding on one order is not a uniform price over a batch, and the two are different mechanisms that the vocabulary distinguishes. Refusing a nearby symbol is what keeps the remaining identity claims in this category meaningful.
paper.residueNote: A venue that admits in writing that its displayed route may not be the best one is telling us the benchmark matters. There is no element for the benchmark, none for who may enter the auction, and none for the affiliation between the auctioneer and the bidders. The construction also arms a prohibition, which is the only place in this category where the algebra objects to anything at all.
